ateret-zekenim/1:_: The debut is interesting. In a house where there is no firstborn there is no need for the eldest to obey. (Maharil) And it is called 'first-born' and there are those who practice redeeming the first-born in the same way that the Omnipresent blesses him in Egypt (DM in the name of everything in him) When a father is a first-born and his son is a first-born, is the first-born to be fasted (from the Haril in the name of the Rashal) that a father who is a priest goes up for his youngest son:
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Shaarei Teshuvah note 1: thus said the Merciful One. NB: it appears to me this depends on the dispute of Rashi and Tosafot in Bechorot daf 49a — for Rashi it depends on viable offspring and the words of Shevut Yaakov fit well; and Tosafot there hold it is a decree of Scripture and even if we know he is viable offspring there is no obligation to redeem until thirty days — and this is as Birkei Yosef, that it is a decree of Scripture; and we rule as Tosafot. And see Yoreh Deah siman 303 [from the Gaon, end of section].
dagul-merevavah/1:_: That is, one born after a definite miscarriage; but if one born after offspring that died within thirty days, which is doubtful miscarriage — since from the Torah we say the majority of offspring are viable, as explained in Even HaEzer siman 164 — even though for chalitzah they require chalitzah, nevertheless regarding the fast of firstborns one may be lenient.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (1) The firstborns fast, etc. Baal brit, sandak, and father of the boy are permitted to eat at the milah and repay the fast afterward (responsum Chut HaShani 25); and it appears when fasting on behalf of the son, even when not baal brit — for this is only a custom; in responsum Nachalat Yaakov siman 10 it does not appear so; in any case one may be lenient to join the minyan. Chok Yaakov wrote: when erev Pesach falls on Shabbat and they fast on Thursday, and a milah occurred on Thursday — he fasts and does not complete, as above siman 559 section 9, unless in countries where they eat the milah meal at night.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: (2) They fast, etc. Sheyarei Knesset HaGedolah wrote: if there is a minyan among them, I would say the shaliach tzibur should say Aneinu in Shema Koleinu; and what they forbade mentioning publicly until Nisan passes — he speaks of one not obligated to fast — end of his words. And I omitted this in Olat Shabbat siman 280 and Magen Avraham here; also in Eliyah Zuta I brought proof from Hagahot Minhagim who wrote they say Aneinu and Birkat Kohanim at Minchah, etc. — see there. At first glance it is difficult: it is simple they say Aneinu on a fast — only it deals with ten in public; and further, since he mentions Birkat Kohanim, evidently a public fast is considered, for on an individual fast one does not say it, as written in Minhagim.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: (3) [Levush] And they do not practice, etc. And Bach wrote it is proper to practice thus — end of his words.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Section 1] The firstborns fast, etc. — and the reason is remembrance of the miracle that they were saved from the plague of firstborns. Tur. Levush. R' Zalman, note 1.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. Whether firstborn from father — as the plague was also on the firstborn to the father. Tur in the name of my father the Rosh. See there note 1; and see below note 16. And Kaf HaChayyim note 2 wrote further the reason: since in any case he is a firstborn for inheritance or opening the womb for redemption — end of his words; and he meant: if a bachelor took a wife who already bore, the first child is firstborn only for inheritance because he is the beginning of his strength; and one who has sons and took a wife who did not bear — the first child is firstborn only for redemption because he is opening the womb, as stated in Yoreh Deah siman 305 section 17 and Choshen Mishpat siman 277 section 8 — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) And accordingly — one born by caesarean section and the one born after him, who is not a firstborn for inheritance or redemption as explained in Yoreh Deah siman 305 and Choshen Mishpat siman 277, need not fast; nevertheless regarding caesarean section this requires further study in law, lest specifically there it was limited from the verse — for regarding inheritance "and they bore him" is written, and regarding redemption "opening the womb" — unlike here, remembrance of the miracle saved from the plague of firstborns, and "firstborn" without qualification applies — this requires further study. Kaf HaChayyim there. And regarding law: since this is only a general concern that perhaps he must fast, he need not fast out of doubt, as stated below notes 6 and 7 — see there. And further see below end of note 8.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Section 2 in the gloss: he fasts on behalf of his son; and this is when the son is not thirty days old, the father need not fast — Korban Netanel, parashat erev Pesach siman 19.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: From the mother. Baer Heitev. And he wrote in Shiyurei Shevet siman 17: one to whom a firstborn son was born on the night of the 14th — if born before midnight, the father must fast for him; but after midnight he does not fast, since the fast is remembrance of the salvation of the firstborns of Israel, and on those born after midnight the decree was not, even on Egyptian firstborns; and he brought proof from the beginning of Avot Rabba: "And it was at midnight," etc., and it is written "on the day the Egyptian," etc. — R' Yehuda said: even though they were struck at midnight, their souls were fluttering in them until morning. And if so, let us interpret "on the day the Egyptian" — those born from midnight onward; if so, on them there was no decree at all, and the first year will be clear, for in any case one need not be stringent in this custom, as Kaf HaChayyim wrote — see there. And in Beit Rachel he questioned this per his view that on a firstborn day-old his father fasts on erev Pesach — if so, what difference if born after midnight of erev Pesach night, since the plague of firstborns was on Pesach night? If so, also on one like this born after midnight of the 14th night there was the decree, only they advance the fast because it is impossible on Yom Tov, etc. But Korban Netanel in any case disagrees with Shevut Yaakov on this and holds that whenever the firstborn is not yet thirty days, one need not fast for him, since he has not left the category of doubtful miscarriage; and is it logical there should be more obligation on the father than redeeming his firstborn son, etc. — and a stringency that leads to leniency is that he fasts in Nisan on Yom Tov without need — end of his words. And in Birkei Yosef he wrote to advocate for Shevut Yaakov: redemption of firstborn is different, for thus said the Merciful One, etc., and one need not be concerned for Nisan and Yom Tov, for so is practiced for publicizing the miracle — see there. And it appears certainly there is no proof from firstborn, as Birkei Yosef wrote; unlike here, where the majority of offspring are not miscarriages, therefore he should fast, for the fast protects him and is remembrance of the salvation of the firstborns of Israel, as stated. And what Shevut Yaakov wrote similarly in Dagul MeRevavah — and see in Shev Yaakov: miscarriage within three months and the form of the offspring is recognizable — the one born after him is firstborn for inheritance and must fast on erev Pesach, as Magen Avraham wrote — see there.
